The 24 tasks comprise 16 core and 8 supplemental tasks. Core tasks also include greeting visitors, helping them enter/leave limousines, cleaning/driving funeral vehicles, pallbearing, procession parking, delivering/moving items, grounds maintenance and memorial charitable-donation advice. entries: Ceremony | Greeting, guidance and escort | Greet guests, guide/escort mourners into viewing rooms or chapels for wakes/funerals, and help them enter/leave limousines.
Caskets and arrangements | Moving, wreaths and lighting | Move caskets into viewing rooms/chapels before ceremonies, arrange wreaths/lighting around them and close caskets at the appropriate stage.

Vehicles and processions | Cleaning, driving and parking | Clean/drive funeral vehicles such as limousines/hearses, join processions, serve as pallbearers, supervise processions and assist cemetery parking.

Venues and equipment | Maintenance, issue and storage | Perform general funeral-home maintenance, care for equipment/grounds, issue/store funeral equipment and transport wreaths/items to burial sites.

Families and donations | Delivery, comfort and advice | Deliver wreaths/items to families, provide comfort/aftercare under institutional arrangements, and advise on charitable gifts in the deceased's name.

Records and assistance | Registration, permits and documents | Under arrangements/authority, assist transport, casketing/cosmetics, obituaries, death registration/burial permits, death certificates/insurance claims, cremation/ashes handling/packaging, and telephone/clerical administration.

Mainland China boundaries | Funeral Administration Regulations revised in 2025 take effect 2026-03-30. Article 25 reserves transport, storage, embalming, cosmetics and cremation of remains to funeral homes. Articles 26 / 28 require death certificates for transport and certificates/confirmation forms for cremation; obvious cause-of-death discrepancies must be reported to police. Institutional assignment does not permit every entity to provide services; titles grant no death-certificate signing power. The Infectious Disease Law revised in 2025 takes effect 2025-09-01; Article 71 distinguishes Category A/anthrax from other infectious-disease deaths and notification, not one universal method. Qualified institutions/staff follow valid technical standards. Information | PIPL6/13/19 checks necessity, grounds/retention; 28 / 29 apply legal sensitivity and applicable separate-consent rules. Article 51 security/powers, 47 no immediate deletion before statutory retention expires; Funeral Regulations 28 require key-area video at least 90 days. Verify external disclosure/publication procedures; invent no family authorization.

Baseline: 16 available, shortfall 18−16=2. A assumes replacement of two faulty items to reach 18 available, with 2 still unverified; no repair has actually occurred. subject.summary: Occupational definition | O*NET-SOC39-4021.00 Funeral Attendants, the fixed Chinese title, move caskets into funeral venues, arrange wreaths and lighting, guide and escort mourners, close caskets, and issue/store equipment. The 24 tasks comprise 16 core and 8 supplemental tasks. Core tasks also include greeting visitors, helping them enter/leave limousines, cleaning/driving funeral vehicles, pallbearing, procession parking, delivering/moving items, grounds maintenance and memorial charitable-donation advice. Supplemental tasks include embalming, dressing, cosmetics/casketing, obituaries, permits/death registration, transporting remains, physician signatures/insurance documents, cremation/ashes, bereavement comfort/counseling/aftercare and administration. These cannot be excluded categorically. Verify actual duties, qualifications and authorization by jurisdiction/institution.
